cards.name: Horizontal Type Tool Myriad Pro Regular 48 pt
cards.id: Presets/Tools/Text.tpl#Horizontal Type Tool Myriad Pro Regular 48 pt
cards.summary: Horizontal Type tool preset, decoded from Text.tpl: Myriad Pro Regular (PostScript name MyriadPro-Regular) at 48 pt, black text (0, 0, 0), left-aligned paragraph, horizontal orientation, automatic leading at 120%, 100% horizontal and vertical scale, metrics kerning, standard ligatures on, language English (stored as englishLanguage). The file also stores tracking 180 (thousandths of an em, unit inferred) and the faux-bold flag on; every one of the 32 presets in this file carries the same two values, so they look unintended rather than part of the font-style / size difference between presets (inferred).
use_for: headlines and large titles set in Myriad Pro Regular (inferred from the size)
starting a text layer with a known font, size and paragraph settings in one click
avoid: it is in an optional library that is not loaded by default, so it does not appear in the Tool Presets panel until the library is loaded

relying on the nominal weight and spacing: with tracking 180 and the faux-bold flag stored, text may come out wider-spaced and heavier than the name suggests (not tested in the app); for a clean start use 'Horizontal Type Tool Myriad Pro Regular 24 pt' from Default Tool Presets (tracking 0, no faux bold) and change font and size
missing fonts: the preset names Myriad Pro; whether it is installed on a given machine was not checked here
cards.applies_to: Horizontal Type tool (typeCreateOrEditTool): sets the font, size, colour and paragraph options for new text layers; it does not restyle existing text on its own (inferred).
cards.how_to_apply: File: <Photoshop 2026 install folder>/Presets/Tools/Text.tpl, entry 'Horizontal Type Tool Myriad Pro Regular 48 pt'. The harvest only parsed this file (its entry is absent from the app's live presetManager list, so the library is not loaded by default) and PGD ran no application route: preset_gallery marks tool presets 'not visual'. Usual route (not observed): Window > Tool Presets, panel menu, pick the 'Text' library from the list at the bottom of the menu (or Load Tool Presets...), then click the preset; it selects the Horizontal Type tool and fills its options. Script route (inferred, not run): app.load(File(<that .tpl>)) to add the library, then an Action Manager 'select' on class toolPreset by name.

cards.name: Circular Rainbow
cards.id: Required/Default Tool Presets.tpl#Circular Rainbow
cards.summary: Gradient tool preset, decoded from Default Tool Presets.tpl: gradient 'Russell's Rainbow' (the same stops as the gradient of that name in the legacy gradient library), blend mode Screen, opacity 90%, gradient-type code 1 (radial, inferred from the name 'Circular'), dither on, transparency on, reverse off (codes GrdD 1 / GrdU 1 / GrdR 0; labels inferred from the key names). Four colour stops sit between 82% and 92% of the gradient length (hue 217, 126, 59, 0 degrees: blue, green, yellow, red) and the opacity starts at 0%, is only 20% at 70% and 80% at 81%, holds 100% from 84% to 89%, then falls to 80% at 92% and 0% at the end, so the colour forms a thin rainbow ring near the outer edge over a faint, mostly clear inner area (read from the stops, not rendered).

lens-flare style arcs and glow rings on a new empty layer
avoid: light backgrounds: Screen blend lightens, so the rainbow barely shows on white or bright areas
painting straight onto a photo layer: apply on a new empty layer so it can be moved or deleted
